Chief_Complaint.content: Painful, cracked palmar skin with intermittent itch
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Painful, cracked palmar skin; intermittent itch

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Palmar skin symptoms began 3–4 months ago and are worsening
Hand symptoms interfere with work and patient has been off work for 3 days
Palmar skin bleeds only when scratched with no spontaneous bleeding
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Bleeds only when scratched; no spontaneous bleeding

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Over-the-counter emollient E45 provided no benefit
Antihistamine provided no benefit for symptoms

Past_Medical_History.content: No prior history of eczema or dermatitis

Family_History.content: No family history of skin disease
No family history of asthma or bowel problems

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a hotel housekeeper
Patient has frequent exposure to cleaning products at work
Patient uses gloves inconsistently at work
Patient had a job change approximately 4 months ago
Patient drinks approximately 2 pints of alcohol per week

Assessment.content: Suspected occupational contact dermatitis of the hands
Hand findings include palmar dry, cracked, and itchy skin
Bleeding from hands occurs only when scratched
There is a temporal relation of symptoms to new job and glove nonuse
Assessment.source_text: temporal relation to new job and glove nonuse

Assessment.content: Over-the-counter emollient and antihistamine were ineffective

Plan_of_Care.content: Patient advised to wear gloves for all cleaning tasks
Plan_of_Care.source_text: wear gloves for all cleaning tasks

Plan_of_Care.content: Start topical steroid cream to affected areas
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Start topical steroid cream to affected areas

Plan_of_Care.content: Use stronger emollients three to four times daily, applied liberally for 10–14 days
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Stronger emollients TID–QID, apply liberally x10–14d

Follow_up_Information.content: Return sooner if rash is spreading or worsening

Review_of_Systems.content: Appetite, eating, and drinking are okay
